notes: Found and fixed a real defect while updating orchestrate-triage-classify.sh's cross-reference: orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh's phase-bucketing switch did not defensively exclude the reserved 'exit_partial' triage group value (it would have fallen through into dispatch-candidate treatment). Added an explicit exit_partial arm to the skip/terminal branch, matching the retired script's own defensive posture for this reserved value.

Added the Phase 6 human-table rendering that Phases 1-7's original implementation pass had omitted: orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh --dry-run now prints the plan JSON on stdout (unchanged, pure single-line JSON in both modes) and a compact human table (Dispatch/Deferred/Blocked/Stop sections, derived from that same JSON object, no second computation) on stderr. Documented the stdout/stderr split in the script's own header. Verified manually and re-ran the full fixture suite (22/22 still pass).

Corrected two batch-orchestration-guardrails.md passages that would have overstated continuity: the retired script's static, one-shot 'out-of-batch unmet predecessor -> exclude' behavior has NO live equivalent in orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh (which mirrors the live cycling engine's uniform per-cycle defer, exactly as Stage MT-3 step 3 always did) -- reworded to mark that specific behavior as purely historical and the live-path gap as still open, rather than falsely claiming the new script inherited it.

grep -rn orchestrate-dry-run-report across the source store now returns exactly 4 hits, all confirmed historical narrative (orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh's own retirement note, batch-admit-schema.md's Version History table, batch-orchestration-guardrails.md's now-explicitly-marked-historical precedent citations, and shell-strict-mode.md's historical Phase 7 migration record).
